IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r3.claim: Al-maʿun here means charity or zakat; the parallel description of hypocrites says they hold back their hands.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p568/r3.anchor: { ويمنعون الماعون } أي الصدقة أو الزكاة

STUDYQURAN:9:67/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r1.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r1.claim: The hypocrites are of their own kind and are not to be counted among believers.
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r1.anchor: that is, they are not to be counted among the believers

STUDYQURAN:9:67/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r2.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r2.claim: One interpretation of clutching their hands shut is reluctance to participate in fighting.
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r2.anchor: Clutching their hands shut refers to their reluctance to take part in fighting (Q)

STUDYQURAN:9:67/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r3.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r3.claim: Another interpretation is reluctance to spend and give in God's way.
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r3.anchor: or to their reluctance to spend and give in the way of God (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:9:67/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r4.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r4.claim: The phrase may encompass both refusing to fight and refusing to give.
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r4.anchor: reluctance to spend and give in the way of God (Ṭ), or both

STUDYQURAN:9:67/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r5.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r5.claim: One reading says they abandoned devotion to God, so He abandoned them without guidance and compassion.
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r5.anchor: They forgot God by abandoning devotion to Him (Ṭ), so He forgot them by abandoning them and leaving them without guidance and compassion

STUDYQURAN:9:67/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r6.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r6.claim: Another reading says they forgot God's remembrance and He acted toward them like one who forgot them.
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r6.anchor: they forgot the remembrance of God, and God acted toward them like one who forgot them (IK)

STUDYQURAN:9:67/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r7.claim: The wording is echoed in the declaration that God forgets people as they forgot the meeting with Judgment Day.
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r7.anchor: Today We forget you just as you forgot the meeting with this your Day

STUDYQURAN:9:67/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r8.claim: The hypocrites invert the Quran's usual ethic of enjoining right and forbidding wrong.
STUDYQURAN:9:67/r8.anchor: Enjoining wrong, forbidding right is an inversion of the usual command in the Quran to enjoin right and forbid wrong

TAB-FULL:v11p548/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r1.claim: Hypocrite men and women profess faith to believers with their tongues while concealing disbelief in God and His Messenger; they are one class and share this pattern.

TAB-FULL:v11p548/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r2.claim: Their command to evil means urging one another to disbelieve in God and Muhammad, reject the revelation, and deny it.

TAB-FULL:v11p548/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r3.claim: They discourage faith in God, His Messenger, and the revelation brought from God.
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r3.anchor: وينهونهم عن الإيمان بالله ورسوله وبما جاءهم به من عند الله

TAB-FULL:v11p548/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r4.claim: They withhold spending for God and charity, denying the people entitled to it the zakat God required from their wealth.
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r4.anchor: ويمسكون أيديهم عن النفقة في سبيل الله

TAB-FULL:v11p548/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r5.claim: Mujāhid glosses their clasped hands as not opening them to spend for what is right.

TAB-FULL:v11p548/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v11p548/r6.claim: Qatāda says they do not open their hands to do good, withholding every good act.

TAB-FULL:v11p550/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p550/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p550/r1.claim: They abandoned obedience to God and following His commands, so God left them without His guidance, direction, or mercy.
TAB-FULL:v11p550/r1.anchor: نسوا من الخير، ولم ينسوا من الشر

TAB-FULL:v11p550/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p550/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p550/r2.claim: Here, as established earlier with supporting examples, forgetting means abandoning or leaving something.
TAB-FULL:v11p550/r2.anchor: نسوا من الخير، ولم ينسوا من الشر

TAB-FULL:v11p550/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p550/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v11p550/r3.claim: Qatāda says they forgot what is good, but did not forget what is evil.
TAB-FULL:v11p550/r3.anchor: نسوا من الخير، ولم ينسوا من الشر

TAB-FULL:v11p550/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p550/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p550/r4.claim: Hypocrites feign faith to believers while concealing disbelief, and thus depart from obedience and from belief in God and His Messenger.
TAB-FULL:v11p550/r4.anchor: هم المفارقون طاعة الله الخارجون عن الإيمان

TABATABAI:9:66-67/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:66-67/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:66-67/r2.claim: The verse indicates that this group had ties and agreement with another group of hypocrites.
TABATABAI:9:66-67/r2.anchor: كما في قوله { المنافقون والمنافقات بعضهم من بعض } الآية

TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r2.claim: Some commentators treat 9:67 as a fresh description of hypocrites' shared traits and fate, followed by a matching description of believers; 9:68's pairing of hypocrites and disbelievers supports their reading.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r2.anchor: ذكروا أنه استئناف يتعرض لحال عامة المنافقين بذكر أوصافهم العامة الجامعة

TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r3.claim: The author instead reads 9:67 as explaining why God may punish one group after saying he may pardon another: all hypocrites share corrupt traits, deeds, and ultimate recompense, so this is not punishment of neighbors for one another's acts.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن الآية في مقام التعليل لقوله في الآية السابقة { إن نعف عن طائفة منكم نعذب طائفة }

TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r4.claim: The phrase expresses a common inner constitution that unifies the hypocrites despite their plurality and makes them share qualities, actions, and the recompense promised by God.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r4.anchor: المنافقين جميعا بعضهم من بعض لاشتراكهم في خبائث الصفات والأعمال

TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r5.claim: Mentioning hypocrite women although none were previously mentioned emphasizes the unity of their disposition with the men and signals women's active place in the corrupt hypocritical society.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r5.anchor: ولعله ذكر المنافقات مع المنافقين مع عدم سبق لذكرهن للدلالة على كمال الاتحاد والاتفاق بينهم

TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r6.claim: The hypocrites promote wrong, obstruct right, and hold back spending in God's path; these habits express their turning away from remembering God and their departure from servitude.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r6.anchor: فهم { يأمرون بالمنكر وينهون عن المعروف } ويمسكون عن الإنفاق في سبيل الله

TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r7.claim: Forgetting God means turning away from his remembrance; God's forgetting them means withholding the reward he gives servants mindful of their Lord.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#4/r7.anchor: نسوا الله تعالى بالإعراض عن ذكره لأنهم فاسقون خارجون عن زي العبودية

TABATABAI:9:64-74#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:64-74#5/r1.claim: Enjoining right, forbidding wrong, and spending in God's path all count as remembrance of God.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#5/r1.anchor: ويتفرع على ذلك أن الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر والإنفاق في سبيل الله من الذكر

TABATABAI:9:64-74#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:64-74#5/r4.claim: The comparison continues the direct address to hypocrites begun at 9:66 and illustrates that they and earlier disbelievers share a nature of turning from God and pursuing worldly enjoyment.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#5/r4.anchor: والآية من تتمة مخاطبة المنافقين التي في قوله { لا تعتذروا قد كفرتم بعد إيمانكم } الآية في سياق واحد متصل

TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r2.speaker: حذيفة
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r2.claim: Hudhayfa says the hypocrites living then were worse than those in the Prophet's time: the earlier ones hid their hypocrisy, while these make it public.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r2.anchor: عن حذيفة قال المنافقون الذين فيكم اليوم شر من المنافقين الذين كانوا على عهد رسول الله

TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r3.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r3.claim: Al-Rida says God neither forgets nor slips; forgetting by God means recompensing those who forgot him by making them forget themselves or leaving them as they neglected preparation for meeting him, as 19:64, 39:19, and 45:34 explain.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r3.anchor: قال سألت الرضا عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل { نسوا الله فنسيهم } فقال إن الله تبارك وتعالى لا ينسى

TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r4.claim: Abu Ja'far explains that they forgot God by abandoning obedience, and God forgot them by abandoning them.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r4.anchor: عن جابر عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام { نسوا الله } قال تركوا طاعة الله { فنسيهم } قال فتركهم

TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r5.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r5.claim: Ali says they forgot God in worldly life by not obeying or believing in him and his Messenger; God forgets them in the afterlife by granting no share in his reward, leaving them deprived of good.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r5.anchor: عن أبي معمر السعداني قال قال علي عليه السلام في قوله { نسوا الله فنسيهم } فإنما يعني

TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r6.claim: The author notes that al-Saduq also transmits Ali's explanation in Ma'ani through Abu Ma'mar.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r6.anchor: أقول ورواه الصدوق في المعاني بإسناده عن أبي معمر عنه عليه السلام

THALABI:v5p65/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p65/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p65/r11.claim: Hypocritical men and women resemble one another, share one religion, and act as a single group.
THALABI:v5p65/r11.anchor: المنافقون والمنافقات بعضهم من بعض أي شكل بعض وعلى دين بعض

THALABI:v5p65/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p65/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p65/r12.claim: They command disbelief and disobedience and forbid faith and obedience.
THALABI:v5p65/r12.anchor: يأمرون بالمنكر بالكفر والمعصية وينهون عن المعروف عن الإيمان والطاعة

THALABI:v5p65/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p65/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p65/r13.claim: They withhold their hands from charity and rightful spending; the author explains the image by noting that a giver extends and opens his hand in good, whereas a miser is said to close it.
THALABI:v5p65/r13.anchor: يمسكونها ويكفونها عن الصدقة والنفقة في الحق ولا يبسطونها بالخير

THALABI:v5p65/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p65/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p65/r14.claim: The hand imagery recalls the statement that the Jews said God's hand was bound, glossed here as held back from spending.
THALABI:v5p65/r14.anchor: ومنه قوله: وقالت اليهود يد الله مغلولة أي ممسكة عن النفقة

THALABI:v5p66/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p66/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p66/r1.claim: Their forgetting God means abandoning obedience; God's forgetting them means withholding worldly guidance and enabling grace and, in the next life, saving mercy from punishment and fire.
THALABI:v5p66/r1.anchor: نسوا الله فنسيهم تركوا طاعة الله فتركهم الله من توفيقه وهدايته في الدنيا

THALABI:v5p66/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p66/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p66/r2.claim: The author states that hypocrites are the disobedient and corrupt ones, then turns to the promised punishment of hypocrites and unbelievers.
THALABI:v5p66/r2.anchor: إن المنافقين هم الفاسقون وعد الله المنافقين والمنافقات والكفار نار جهنم

THALABI:v5p67/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p67/r1.speaker: حذيفة
THALABI:v5p67/r1.claim: Hudhayfa says hypocrites openly declaring their hypocrisy in his day are worse than those in the Prophet's time, who had concealed it.
THALABI:v5p67/r1.anchor: وقال حذيفة: المنافقون الذين فيكم اليوم شر من المنافقين الذي كانوا على عهد النبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r1.claim: The hypocrites are of one another in religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (أي على دين بعض)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r2.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r2.claim: They mix with and ally themselves to one another; this means neither descent nor birth, since believers and hypocrites can each descend from the other group.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: (أي بعضهم يلابس بعضا، ويوالي بعضا، وليس المعنى على النسل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r3.claim: The phrase follows their claim that they are among the believers, and means the hypocrites are not believers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (هذا يتلو قوله: {ويحلفون بالله إنهم لمنكم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r4.speaker: غيره من أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r4.claim: They are affiliated with one another through shared hypocrisy: their affair is one and inseparable.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r4.anchor: وقال غيره من أهل المعاني: (معنى {بعضهم من بعض} يضاف إلى بعض بالاجتماع على النفاق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r5.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r5.claim: They command hypocrisy, discourage jihad in God's path, and deny the Messenger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r5.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (يريد: بالنفاق والتثبيط عن الجهاد في سبيل الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r7.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives the same explanation as al-Dahhak: commanding disbelief in Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p540/r7.anchor: وقال الضحاك: (يأمرون بالكفر بمحمد) (¬5)، ونحوه قال الزجاج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (عن اتباع رسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r2.speaker: عطاء عنه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r2.claim: They discourage sincerity to God with a truthful intention.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r2.anchor: وقال عطاء عنه: (الإخلاص لله بنية صادقة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r4.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r4.claim: They discourage Islam and giving alms to the Messenger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك: (عن الإسلام وأداء الصدقات إلى رسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r5.claim: They withhold wealth from spending in God's path; al-Hasan and Mujahid agree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (عن النفقة في سبيل الله)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r6.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r6.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid share Ibn Abbas's gloss that they withhold from spending in God's path.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r7.claim: They do not extend their hands in any good.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r8.speaker: القرظي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r8.claim: They withhold their hands from every good.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r8.anchor: وقال القرظي: (يقبضون أيديهم عن كل خير)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r9.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r9.claim: They neither give charity nor pay alms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r9.anchor: وقال الزجاج: (أي: لا يصدقون ولا يزكون)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r10.claim: Since a giver extends his hand when giving, a miser who withholds is described as having clenched his hand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p541/r10.anchor: المعطي يمد يده ويبسطها بالعطاء، فقيل لمن بخل ومنع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r1.claim: They abandoned obedience, including jihad; God then abandoned them and left them in the doubt in their hearts.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r2.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r2.claim: They abandoned God's command, so He left them deprived of every good.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك: ([تركوا أمر الله فتركهم من كل خير)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r3.claim: They neglected God's command as though it were forgotten through inattention; He repaid them by making them forgotten from His reward and mercy, in a verbal pairing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r3.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: (معناه:] (¬5): تركوا أمره حتى صار بمنزلة المنسي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r4.claim: The hypocrites are disobedient to God and have departed from His command and obedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p543/r4.anchor: أي: العاصون الله (¬7) والخارجون عن أمره وطاعته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p547#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p547#2/r7.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p547#2/r7.claim: Hypocrites are affiliated only through shared hypocrisy and lack believers' mutual loyalty because their hearts differ; believers instead have loving, compassionate unity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p547#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعاني: [ذكر الله المنافقين] (6)، فقال: {بعضهم من بعض} وذكر المؤمنين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r1.claim: Hypocritical men and women share one religion.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r2.claim: Their commanding what is wrong means calling people to disbelieve in Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r2.anchor: بالكفر بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r3.claim: Their forbidding what is right means discouraging people from following Muhammad.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r4.claim: They withhold their money from spending in God's cause.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r5.claim: They abandoned God's commands, so He left them deprived of all good and forsook them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r5.anchor: تركوا أمر الله، فتركهم من كل خير وخذلهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:67-68/r6.claim: The hypocrites are those who depart from what God commanded.

ELMALILI:9:64-70/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:64-70/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:64-70/r3.claim: Elmalılı renders the hypocrites' clasping of their hands as keeping their hands tightly closed, conveying that they withhold their hands.
ELMALILI:9:64-70/r3.anchor: münkeri emr, ma‘ruftan nehyederler ve ellerini sıkı tutarlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:61/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:61/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:61/r15.claim: The account contrasts the hypocrites' character and fate in verses 67–68 with the believers' character and happy outcome in verses 71–72.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:61/r15.anchor: 67. âyette münafık karakterine ve 68. âyette münafıkların acı âkıbetlerine değinildiği gibi, 71. âyette mümin karakterine ve 72. âyette de onların mutlu sonlarına işaret edilerek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r1.claim: Men and women are separately named in 9:71, as in 9:67, because each verse describes the shared traits of both sexes in its group.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r1.anchor: Münafıklardan söz edilirken 67. âyette erkeğiyle kadınıyla münafık karakterine işaret edilmek üzere her iki cins ayrı ayrı zikredilmişti. 71. âyette de müminlerin ortak niteliklerine değinildiğinden erkek ve kadınları ayrı ayrı anılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r2.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r2.claim: Razi's comparison says hypocrites promote evil and restrain good, whereas sincere believers encourage good and try to turn people away from evil.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r2.anchor: İki yüzlü davranan kimselere hâkim olan özellik, kötülükleri körükleyip iyilikten alıkoymak iken yürekten inananların temel vasfı iyiliği özendirmek, kötülükten vazgeçirmeye çalışmaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r3.claim: Hypocrites are tight-fisted in God's cause, while believers pay zakat, give generously beyond it, and regret being unable to give more.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r3.anchor: Münafıklar Allah yolunda harcamada eli sıkı davranırken müminler zekâtlarını verirler ve ayrıca cömertçe gönüllü bağışlarda bulunurlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r4.claim: Hypocrites approach prayer reluctantly, while believers pray sincerely, with an inner desire and sense of duty.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r4.anchor: Münafıklar namaza üşenerek gelirler, müminler ise namazlarını bir kulluk vecîbesi sayarak içten gelen bir istekle kılarlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r5.claim: When called to fight for God, hypocrites evade with excuses, but believers give their lives and wealth and answer without faltering.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r5.anchor: Allah yolunda savaşmak gerektiğinde münafıklar türlü mazeretlerle yan çizmeye çalışırlar, müminler ise canlarını ve mallarını esirgemeden böyle bir çağrıya koşarlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r6.claim: Hypocrites disregard God and His message and mock believers, while believers obey God and His Messenger fully.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:71/r6.anchor: Münafıklar Allah’ı ve O’nun mesajını umursamazlar, O’na ve vaad ettiklerine candan inanan müminlerle alay ederler, müminler ise Allah ve resulüne mutlak itaat gösterirler

QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r2.claim: Believers strengthen one another, whereas hypocrites mutually support one another like birds alighting among their own flock, helping companions persist in corruption and blinding them to guidance.
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r2.anchor: فالمنافق لصاحبه أس به قوامه ، وأصل به قيامه ؛ يعينه على فساده ، ويعمي عليه طريق رشاده

QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r3.claim: A believer helps another see personal faults, makes sins hateful, supports the person on the right path, and distances them from corruption.
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r3.anchor: ويبغض لديه ويقبح - في عينيه - ذنوبه ، وهو على السداد ينجده ، وعن الفساد يبعده

QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r4.claim: The hypocrites’ withholding of their hands means that they do not ask God for their needs.
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r4.anchor: عن طلب الحوائج من الله تعالى

QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r5.claim: God’s forgetting them is requital for their forgetting Him: they abandoned obedience and chose disobedience, so He left them to what they chose.
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r5.anchor: جازاهم على نسيانهم ، فسمى جزاء النسيان نسيانا . تركوا طاعته ، وآثروا مخالفته

QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r6.claim: Qushayri explains God’s abandonment by linking it to the description of people left in darkness, unable to see.
QUSHAYRI:v1p432/r6.anchor: قال تعالى : { وتركهم فى ظلمات لا يبصرون }

BAQILLANI:v1p63/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p63/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p63/r1.claim: Human convention and instruction may establish the basic language, while people discover, imitate, and refine particular forms of discourse; this does not explain Quranic inimitability.
BAQILLANI:v1p63/r1.anchor: إن التواضع وقع على أصل الباب وكذلك التوقيف ولم يقع على فنون تصرف الخطاب

BAQILLANI:v1p63/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p63/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p63/r2.claim: The Arabs' inability to imitate the Quran despite understanding composition, facing a challenge, and needing to answer proves it exceeds customary speech and is a prophetic miracle.
BAQILLANI:v1p63/r2.anchor: فاستدللنا بتحيرهم في أمر القرآن على خروجه عن عادة كلامهم ووقوعه موقعا يخرق العادات وهذه سبيل المعجزات

BAQILLANI:v1p63/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p63/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p63/r3.claim: The Arabs readily produced elaborate poetry on subjects with no worldly or religious use and competed in eloquence, so lack of skill cannot explain their failure to answer the challenge.
BAQILLANI:v1p63/r3.anchor: ثم كانوا يتفاخرون باللسن والذلاقة والفصاحة والذرابة ويتنافرون فيه

BURHAN:v2p229/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p229/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p229/r4.claim: The reproachful address forms يا أيها الذين كفروا and قل يا أيها الكافرون occur only in these two Qur’anic places because the form itself humiliates.
BURHAN:v2p229/r4.anchor: ولتضمنه الإهانة لم يقع في القرآن في غير هذين الموضعين

BURHAN:v3p381/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p381/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p381/r1.claim: Istihza is making an insult heard, while sukhriya may be inward; the prophets’ wording uses mockery rather than the literal insulting act, which is not their conduct.
BURHAN:v3p381/r1.anchor: والجواب أن الاستهزاء هو إسماع الإساءة والسخرية قد تكون في النفس ولهذا يقولون سخرت منه

BURHAN:v4p424/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p424/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p424/r7.claim: Min in the statement that male and female hypocrites are of one another means association and allegiance, not descent, since children of hypocrites may be believers and vice versa.
BURHAN:v4p424/r7.anchor: اي يلابس بعضهم بعضا ويواليه وليس المعنى على النسل والولادة

BURHAN:v1p22/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p22/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p22/r1.claim: Exegetes valued occasions of revelation and wrote dedicated works; Ali ibn al-Madini and especially al-Wahidi are named, and the subject is not merely history.
BURHAN:v1p22/r1.anchor: وقد اعتنى بذلك المفسرون في كتبهم وأفردوا فيه تصانيف منهم علي بن المديني شيخ البخاري

BURHAN:v1p22/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p22/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p22/r2.claim: Knowing an occasion can reveal the wisdom that prompted a legal ruling.
BURHAN:v1p22/r2.anchor: منها وجه الحكمة الباعثة على تشريع الحكم

BURHAN:v1p22/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p22/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p22/r3.claim: For those who hold that the ruling follows the specific cause, the occasion can restrict the ruling to that cause.
BURHAN:v1p22/r3.anchor: ومنها تخصيص الحكم به عند من يرى أن العبرة بخصوص السبب

BURHAN:v1p22/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p22/r4.speaker: أبو الفتح القشيري
BURHAN:v1p22/r4.claim: Al-Qushayri calls knowledge of the occasion a strong path to understanding the Qur’an; Companions gained it from contextual clues surrounding events.
BURHAN:v1p22/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو الفتح القشيري بيان سبب النزول طريق قوى فى فهم معانى الكتاب العزيز

BURHAN:v1p22/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p22/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p22/r5.claim: When general wording has evidence for restriction, the case that occasioned it cannot be excluded by interpretation or consensus; its inclusion is certain, and earlier occasions affect later general wording.
BURHAN:v1p22/r5.anchor: فإن محل السبب لا يجوز إخراجه بالاجتهاد والإجماع كما حكاه القاضي أبو بكر

BURHAN:v1p22/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p22/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p22/r6.claim: The author rejects excluding the original case: it would delay explanation beyond need or turn from the question asked; the occasion definitively affects its case and may also weaken or defeat implications beyond it.
BURHAN:v1p22/r6.anchor: أحدهما أنه يلزم منه تأخير البيان عن وقت الحاجة ولا يجوز والثاني أن فيه عدولا عن محل السؤال

BURHAN:v2p449/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p449/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p449/r1.claim: For divine attributes also borne by others, the source's received usage leaves the description grammatically dependent rather than detached.
BURHAN:v2p449/r1.anchor: ونظير ذلك في صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى مما يتصف به غيره فلذلك لم يقطع

SULAMI:v1p279#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r1.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq contrasts hypocrites, who conceal one another's faults, with believers, who serve as mirrors through which one sees defects and receives correction aiding salvation.
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : المنافق ستر المنافق يستر عليه عوراته

SULAMI:v1p279#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r2.claim: Some interpret the hypocrites' closed hands as withholding them from raising supplications and requests to their Patron; a report about the Prophet at the standing, with hand to chest like a beggar, and an accompanying poem illustrate the plea.
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : يقبضون أيديهم عن رفعها إلى مولاها في الدعوات والحوائج

SULAMI:v1p279#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r3.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes their closed hands as refusal to give charity.

SULAMI:v1p279#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r4.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r4.claim: A further interpretation takes their closed hands as refusing to help Muslims.
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r4.anchor: وقيل : يقبضون أيديهم عن معونة المسلمين

SULAMI:v1p279#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r5.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r5.claim: Sahl explains their forgetting God as forgetting His blessings, after which God makes them forget to give thanks for those blessings.
SULAMI:v1p279#3/r5.anchor: قال سهل : نسوا نعم الله عندهم فأنساهم الله شكر النعم

ITQAN:v2p341/r40.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p341/r40.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p341/r40.claim: Their forgetting God means abandoning obedience to Him.

ITQAN:v2p341/r41.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p341/r41.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p341/r41.claim: God’s forgetting them means withholding His reward and honor.

ITQAN:v3p307/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p307/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p307/r6.claim: Hypocrites share doubt and hypocrisy but lack common open allegiance; believers and declared unbelievers aid one another, unlike the hypocrites whose hearts are divided.
ITQAN:v3p307/r6.anchor: لأن المنافقين ليسوا متناصرين على دين معين وشريعة ظاهرة

ITQAN:v4p341/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p341/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p341/r1.claim: The passage catalogs textual signs that an act is forbidden, including that God makes the act a cause for forgetting its doer; a question about the reason for an act indicates prohibition more clearly than mere dislike.
ITQAN:v4p341/r1.anchor: جعله الله سببا لنسيانه فاعله أو وصفه نفسه بالصبر عليه أو بالحلم أو بالصفح عنه

TUSTARI:9:67/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:9:67/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:9:67/r1.claim: Forgetting God means forgetting His blessings, so He makes them forget to give thanks for those blessings.
TUSTARI:9:67/r1.anchor: يعني نسوا نعم الله عندهم، فأنساهم شكر النعم

DAMGHANI:v1p357/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p357/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p357/r9.claim: Fāsiqūn can mean those who disbelieve in the Prophet and what he brought; Dāmghānī links the hypocrisy passage with another condemnation of them.
DAMGHANI:v1p357/r9.anchor: ان المنافقين هم الفاسقون يعني في كفرهم بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وبما جاء به

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba says fisq in the language means going outside or departing from something.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : الفسق في اللغة : الخروج عن الشيء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ connects the word to a date that splits out of its skin.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r2.anchor: قال الفراء : ومنه يقال : فسقت الرطبة إذا خرجت من قشرها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r3.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r3.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī called a mouse fuwaysiqa, a diminutive of fāsiqa.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r3.anchor: وحكى ابن فارس : عن ابن الأعرابي : الفويسقة : الفأرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r4.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r4.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says fāsiq was not heard in pre-Islamic poetry or speech, an unusual absence for an Arabic word.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r4.anchor: قال : ولم يسمع في كلام الجاهلية في شعر ولا في كلام : فاسق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r9.claim: Some exegetes add a fifth sense: violating the Messenger's command.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p464/r9.anchor: وقد ألحق بعضهم وجها خامسا ، فقال : والفسق : مخالفة أمر الرسول

FARRA:v1p445/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p445/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p445/r1.claim: Their withholding their hands means refusing to spend on the Prophet.
FARRA:v1p445/r1.anchor: يمسكون عن النفقة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p189#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p189#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p189#2/r1.claim: Their forgetting God means abandoning God's command; God's forgetting them means leaving them to their fate.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p189#2/r1.anchor: {نسوا الله فنسيهم} أي تركوا أمر الله فتركهم.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p106/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p106/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p106/r1.claim: The metaphor's source is a stairway: one ascends or descends rung by rung, and this concrete sense is borrowed for درجات.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p106/r1.anchor: من الدرجة، وذلك أن الراقي فيها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p106/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p106/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p106/r2.claim: ويقبضون أيديهم means withholding gifts; the image comes from a giver extending and opening a hand, so a miser is said to close his hand.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p106/r2.anchor: وأصل هذا: أن المعطي بيده يمدها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r7.speaker: النبي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r7.claim: In a prayer against someone who satirized him, the Prophet asked for a curse matching the number or place of the satire, meaning requital for it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r7.anchor: قول النبي) صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اللهم إن فلانا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r8.claim: God's forgetting the hypocrites means leaving or requiting them, using their own forgetfulness of God as reciprocal language.

NAHHAS:v2p227/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p227/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p227/r1.claim: بعضهم is a subject; alternatively, the second بعضهم begins a new subject and من بعض is its predicate.
NAHHAS:v2p227/r1.anchor: ابتداء ( بعضهم ) ابتداء ثان ويجوز أن يكون بدلا ويكون الخبر من بعض

NAHHAS:v2p227/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p227/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p227/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq links this to their claim they belong to the believers, while they do not; they resemble each other in urging wrong, forbidding right, and withholding from jihad.
NAHHAS:v2p227/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق هذا متصل بقوله ويحلفون بالله إنهم لمنكم وما هم منكم أي ليسوا من المؤمنين ولكن بعضهم من بعض

SAMIN-DURR:9:67/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:67/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:67/r1.claim: The clause يأمرون and its coordinated clauses have no syntactic position; they explain بعضهم من بعض.
SAMIN-DURR:9:67/r1.anchor: هذه الجملة لا محل لها لأنها مفسرة لقوله { بعضهم من بعض } وكذلك ما عطف على " يأمرون "

ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r1.claim: This continues the statement that they swear they are among the believers and clarifies that hypocrites are not believers.
ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r1.anchor: هذا يتلو قوله تعالى: (يحلفون بالله إنهم لمنكم). أي ليس المنافقون من المؤمنين

ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r2.claim: They command disbelief in the Prophet and forbid belief in him.
ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r2.anchor: أي يأمرون بالكفر بالنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -.

ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r3.claim: They hold back their hands by not giving alms or paying zakat.

ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r4.claim: They abandoned God's command, so God left them without His mercy and guidance.
ZAJJAJ:v2p460/r4.anchor: أي تركوا أمر الله فتركهم الله من رحمته وتوفيقه.

ASAD-NOTES:9:65#n94/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:65#n94/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:9:65#n94/r1.claim: The hypocrites' behavior is effectively the reverse of what is expected of believers; Asad cites 3:104, 3:110, 3:114, 9:71, 9:112, and 22:41.
ASAD-NOTES:9:65#n94/r1.anchor: their behaviour is - in its effect, at least - the exact opposite of that expected of the believers

ASAD-NOTES:9:65#n95/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:65#n95/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:9:65#n95/r1.claim: These verses concern deliberate hypocrites identified in 9:66, not wavering people whose hypocrisy arises from inner fears and uncertainty.
ASAD-NOTES:9:65#n95/r1.anchor: this and the following verses refer to the conscious hypocrites spoken of in the last sentence of the preceding verse, and not to the waverers

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r1.claim: Zulm means exceeding bounds and ranges in degree up to kufr; kufr itself means leaving the faith.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r1.anchor: المعروف أن الظلم هو مجاوزة الحد والكفر هو الخروج عن الملة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r2.claim: Fisq means leaving obedience to God; the word is likened to a date that comes out of its husk.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r2.anchor: الفسق هو الخروج عن طاعة الله تعالى وله مراتب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r3.claim: Zulm commonly involves violating others' rights, whereas fisq is broader: every oppressor is a fasiq, but a fasiq may only wrong himself.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r3.anchor: الظلم أخذ حقوق الغير والفسق عام، وكل ظالم فاسق وليس كل فاسق ظالم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r4.claim: Fisq has degrees and can reach kufr, as with Iblis; the Qur'an also calls disbelievers fasiqin, while some fisq does not reach disbelief.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r4.anchor: الفسق درجات أيضا وله مراتب حتى يصل إلى الكفر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1093/r5.claim: Fisq can describe wrongdoing that is not disbelief, as in the prohibition of indecency and quarrelling during pilgrimage.

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.claim: Interrogative من can mark number like أي: forms include منين for two or males, منه for a woman, منتين for two women, and منات for women plural.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.anchor: اعلم أنك تثنى من إذا قلت رأيت رجلين كما تثنى أيا

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.claim: In singular oblique contexts من has forms منو and مني, while أي behaves like fully declinable names in pause because it takes tanwin in the relative construction.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.anchor: إلا أن الواحد يخالف أيا في موضع الجر والرفع

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.claim: Al-Khalīl says the nūn in the forms of من is silent in connected speech; من يا فتى shows this relative construction.

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.claim: Al-Khalīl adduces منو in pause followed by من يا فتى to show the connected form works like من قال ذاك and can refer to a group.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.anchor: وزعم الخليل رحمه الله أن الدليل على ذلك أنك تقول منو في الوقف ثم تقول من

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.claim: أي can be pluralized, dualized, and added in the relative construction, whereas interrogative من does none of these; أي is stronger because it also takes tanwin and iḍāfa.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.anchor: وأي منون على كل حال في الاستفهام وغيره فهو أقوى

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.claim: Sībawayh records Yūnus's report that some speakers keep من forms unchanged in pause regardless of number.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.anchor: منا ومني ومنو عنيت واحدا أو اثنين أو جميعا في الوقف

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.claim: Yūnus proposes منه analogized on أية as منة, but Sībawayh calls this distant and says it was heard only once in poetry.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.anchor: وأما يونس فإنه [ كان ] يقيس منه على أية

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.claim: Yūnus says he heard a Bedouin say ضرب من منا, then acknowledged not everyone accepted the form.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.anchor: وكان يونس إذا ذكرها يقول لا يقبل هذا كل أحد

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.claim: Sībawayh rejects the form as distant and says it is not widely used by Arabs.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.anchor: وهذا بعيد لا تكلم به العرب

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.claim: When asking about a woman and man, the first-mentioned gender determines whether the form is من / منا or من / منه.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.anchor: فبدأت في المسألة بالمؤنث قلت من

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكتثنىمنإذاقلترأيترجلينكما.claim: أي is pluralized in interrogative use because that is its main and original use; it behaves there like a complete noun, while من only partly parallels it.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p188/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p188/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p188/r3.claim: When نسي means leave, attributing it to God is figurative: people leave obedience and God leaves them without mercy or rescue; the Qurʾan also uses ترك for leaving people alone.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p188/r3.anchor: فمن الترك قوله: نسوا الله فنسيهم [التوبة/ 67] أي: تركوا

NASHR:v2p140/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p140/r8.speaker: جميع القراء
NASHR:v2p140/r8.claim: Although the waw is said to be omitted in the rasm of نسوا الله فنسيهم, the common reading tradition pauses with waw.
NASHR:v2p140/r8.anchor: وأما نسوا الله فنسيهم، فقد ذكر القراء أنه حذف أيضا رسما وسائر الناس على خلافه وعدوا ذلك، وهما منه فيوقف عليه بالواو للجميع

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p283/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p283/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p283/r1.claim: Qatāda says they hold back their hands from every good deed.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p283/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ويقبضون أيديهم ﴾ قال يقبضون أيديهم عن كل خير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r8.claim: “Some are of others” describes their shared judgment, rank, and hypocrisy, not literal partiality; they follow one religion and are not believers, as 9:56 says.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r8.anchor: بل بعضهم من بعض في الحكم والمنزلة والنفاق، فهم على دين واحد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r9.claim: Their wrongdoing includes disbelief, worship of other than God, and sins; the people addressed lacked power and visible activity because Islam was ascendant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r9.anchor: ووصفهم بخلاف ما عليه المؤمنون من أنهم يأمرون بالمنكر وهو الكفر وعبادة غير الله والمعاصي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r10.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains “withhold their hands” as refusing to spend in God's cause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r10.anchor: وقبض الأيدي عبارة عن عدم الإنفاق في سبيل الله قاله الحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r11.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r11.claim: Qatāda takes the phrase as withholding every kind of good.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says they withhold from jihad and carrying arms against the enemies of religion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r12.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: عن الجهاد وحمل السلاح في قتال أعداء الدين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r13.speaker: سفيان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r13.claim: Sufyān interprets the phrase as refraining from raising hands in supplication.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r13.anchor: وقال سفيان: عن الرفع في الدعاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r14.claim: Another view takes the phrase as a metaphor for stinginess with expenditure on obligatory and other good causes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r14.anchor: وقيل ذلك كناية عن الشح في النفقات في المبار والواجبات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r16.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r16.claim: Qatāda says they abandoned obedience to God and His Messenger, so God abandoned them from good, while not forgetting them in punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r16.anchor: قال قتادة: تركوا طاعة الله وطاعة رسوله فنسيهم، أي: تركهم من الخير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r17.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r17.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says they neglected God's remembrance, so He left them without mercy and grace; “forgetting” emphatically expresses abandonment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r17.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أغفلوا ذكره فنسيهم تركهم من رحمته وفضله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r18.claim: They are the fully realized fāsiqūn, whose rebellion has reached its full extent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p455/r18.anchor: هم الفاسقون أي: هم الكاملون في الفسق

ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r1.claim: The hypocrite men and women resemble one another in hypocrisy as parts of one thing, sharing the same nature and outward form; this gathers up their previously described faults.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r1.anchor: أي متشابهون في النفاق كتشابه أبعاض الشيء الواحد والمراد الاتحاد في الحقيقة والصورة

ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r2.claim: The clause may connect with the hypocrites' oath that they are among the believers and refute it by affirming 'they are not of you'; alternatively it summarizes all their faults. In either construction, min expresses connection, as in the hadith 'You are to me as Aaron was to Moses.'
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r2.anchor: وقيل : هي متصلة بقوله تعالى : ( يحلفون بالله إنهم لمنكم ) والمراد منها تكذيب قولهم

ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r3.claim: Explicitly mentioning the women signals how deeply rooted the group is in disbelief and hypocrisy.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r3.anchor: والتعرض لأحوال الإناث للإيذان بكمال عراقتهم في الكفر والنفاق

ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r4.claim: Their commanding wrong means urging denial of the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r4.anchor: أي بالتكذيب بالنبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, as reported by Ibn Abi Hatim, identifies the good they suppress as the testimony that there is no god but God and acknowledgment of what God revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r5.anchor: كما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r6.claim: Abu al-Aliya says every instance of munkar in the Quran means worship of idols and Satan; al-Alusi allows the terms here to include those examples and other wrongs and goods.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r6.anchor: وأخرج عن أبي العالية أنه قال : كل منكر ذكر في القرآن المراد منه عبادة الأوثان والشيطان

ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r7.claim: The clause may stand independently to reinforce what came before and reveal how they oppose believers, or serve as a second predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r7.anchor: والجملة استئناف مقرر لمضمون ما سبق مفصح عن مضادة حالهم لحال المؤمنين أو خبر ثان

ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r8.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r8.claim: Qatada and al-Hasan explain the phrase as withholding expenditure in obedience to God; clasping the hand is a metaphor for stinginess, just as extending it signifies generosity.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r8.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن وقبض اليد كناية عن الشح والبخل كما أن بسطها كناية عن الجود

ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r9.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r9.claim: Al-Jubba'i says the phrase means holding back from jihad, but al-Alusi rejects this as contrary to the common usage of the expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r9.anchor: وعن الجبائي أن المراد يمسكون أيديهم عن الجهاد في سبيل الله تعالى وهو خلاف الشائع

ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r10.claim: Forgetting God is metaphorical for abandoning obedience to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r10.anchor: النسيان مجاز عن الترك وهو كناية عن ترك الطاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r11.claim: God's forgetting them means withholding His grace and favor; the wording echoes their own forgetting by way of verbal correspondence.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r11.anchor: منع لطفه وفضله عنهم والتعبير بالنسيان للمشاكلة

ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r12.claim: They are the most complete in rebellion and departure from obedience, rhetorically described as though they were the whole category; the restriction is justified by the separating pronoun and definite predicate despite other sinners.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p132/r12.anchor: الكاملون في التمرد والفسق الذي هو الخروج عن الطاعة والانسلاخ عن كل حتى كأنهم الجنس كله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r1.claim: The hypocrite men and women share one religion; another explanation is that their affair is unified through collective hypocrisy.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r1.anchor: أي: هم على دين واحد. وقيل: أمرهم واحد بالاجتماع على النفاق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r2.anchor: بالشرك والمعصية، {وينهون عن المعروف} أي عن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r3.anchor: وينهون عن المعروف} أي عن الإيمان والطاعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r4.claim: They withhold their hands from charity and spending in God's cause, refusing to extend them in good.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r4.anchor: يمسكونها عن الصدقة والإنفاق في سبيل الله ولا يبسطونها بخير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r5.claim: They abandoned obedience to God, so He withheld guidance in this world and mercy in the next, leaving them in punishment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r5.anchor: تركوا طاعة الله، فتركهم الله من توفيقه وهدايته في الدنيا، ومن رحمته في الآخرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p71#2/r6.claim: The verse concludes that the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient.

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r1.claim: Hypocrite men and women resemble one another in hypocrisy and distance from faith, like parts of one thing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r1.anchor: متشابهة في النفاق والبعد عن الإيمان

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r2.claim: Alternatively, this rebuts their oath that they belong to believers and confirms they do not; their conduct demonstrates the opposition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r2.anchor: وقيل إنه تكذيب لهم في حلفهم بالله إنهم لمنكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r3.claim: They command unbelief and sins and forbid faith and obedience.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r3.anchor: وينهون عن المعروف } عن الإيمان والطاعة

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r4.claim: Withholding their hands is an idiom for miserliness.

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r5.claim: They neglected remembrance of God and obedience to Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r5.anchor: غفلوا عن ذكر الله وتركوا طاعته

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r6.claim: God’s “forgetting” means withholding His favor and grace.

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r7.claim: They are fully given to rebellion and departure from the sphere of good.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:67-68/r7.anchor: الكاملون في التمرد والفسوق عن دائرة الخير

BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r10.claim: Male and female hypocrites share one nature, like a single body, resembling each other in every act and condition through shared desire, habit, custom, and imitation.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r10.anchor: أي في صفة النفاق هم فيها كالجسد الواحد , أمورهم متشابهة في أقوالهم وأفعالهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r11.claim: They promote mischief and other vile conduct, oppose what honors Islam and its people, and do so to stir up discord.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r11.anchor: أي مما تقدم من الخبال والإيضاع في الخلال وغير ذلك من سيء الخصال

BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r12.claim: They clutch back their wealth and spend only reluctantly.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r12.anchor: أي يحشون فلا ينفقون إلا وهم كارهون

BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r13.claim: Their forgetting God means treating the supreme sovereign as irrelevant; His “forgetting” them is leaving them outside mercy, bringing punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r13.anchor: فعل بهم فعل الناسي لما استهان به بأن تركهم من رحمة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r14.claim: They alone are fully characterized as fāsiqūn: firmly outside the sphere of obedience that benefits them.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r14.anchor: أي الخارجون عن دائرة ما ينفعهم من الطاعة الراسخون في ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r15.claim: Because all hypocrites share one character, the unpardoned men would have behaved the same way if they had gone on campaign.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p343/r15.anchor: فقد علم أنهم لو غزوا فعلوا هؤلاء سواء لأن الكل من طينة واحدة

DURR-FULL:v4p232/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r1.speaker: حذيفة
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r1.claim: Ḥudhayfa defines a hypocrite as someone who professes Islam but does not act by it.
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r1.anchor: عن حذيفة أنه سئل عن المنافق فقال: الذي يصف الإسلام ولا يعمل به

DURR-FULL:v4p232/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan distinguishes hypocrisy of denying Muḥammad, which is unbelief, from hypocrisy of sins and offenses, whose perpetrator may be hoped for.
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r2.anchor: عن الحسن قال: النفاق نفاقان نفاق تكذيب بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فذاك كفر ونفاق خطايا وذنوب فذاك يرجى لصاحبه

DURR-FULL:v4p232/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says enjoining wrong is denial, the worst wrong, while forbidding good is rejecting the testimony of God's oneness and what He revealed, the greatest good.
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {يأمرون بالمنكر} قال: هو التكذيب قال: وهو أنكر المنكر {وينهون عن المعروف} قال: شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله والإقرار بما أنزل الله

DURR-FULL:v4p232/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says every Qur'anic mention of munkar means worship of idols and Satan.
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال: كل آية ذكرها الله تعالى في القرآن فذكر المنكر عبادة الأوثان والشيطان

DURR-FULL:v4p232/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r5.claim: Mujāhid says they do not open their hands to spend in what God requires.
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {ويقبضون أيديهم} قال: لا يبسطونها بنفقة في حق الله

DURR-FULL:v4p232/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r6.claim: Qatāda says they do not extend their hands to good; they forget every good but do not forget evil, and God forgets them.
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r6.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {ويقبضون أيديهم} قال: لا يبسطونها بخير {نسوا الله فنسيهم} قال: نسوا من كل خير ولم ينسوا من الشر

DURR-FULL:v4p232/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they abandoned God, so He deprived them of His honor and reward.
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {نسوا الله فنسيهم} قال: تركوا الله فتركهم من كرامته وثوابه

DURR-FULL:v4p232/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r8.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says they abandoned God's command, so He left them without His mercy and without granting faith and righteous deeds.
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك {نسوا الله} قال: تركوا أمر الله {فنسيهم} تركهم من رحمته أن يعطيهم إيمانا وعملا صالحا

DURR-FULL:v4p232/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r9.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says God does not literally forget His creatures; He forgets them with respect to good on Resurrection Day.
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r9.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في الآية قال: إن الله لا ينسى من خلقه ولكن نسيهم من الخير يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v4p232/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r10.claim: Mujāhid says they are forgotten in the punishment.
DURR-FULL:v4p232/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: نسوا في العذاب

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains munkar as denial and calls it the most abominable wrong.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس يعني قوله : المنكر : هو التكذيب وهو انكر المنكر

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliyah says that wherever the Quran mentions munkar, it means worship of idols and Satan.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r2.anchor: عن أبيه عن الربيع عن أبي العالية قال : كل آية ذكرها الله في القران فذكر المنكر : عبادة الاوثان والشيطان

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r3.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan glosses munkar as disobedience to their Lord.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r3.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : المنكر قال : معصية ربهم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the recognized good is professing God's oneness, affirming revelation, and fighting for it; there is no greater good than the testimony of faith.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، المعروف ، ان تشهدوا ان لا اله الا الله والاقرار بما انزل الله وتقاتلونهم عليه ولا اله الا الله هو اعظم المعروف

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliyah glosses the recognized good as God's oneness.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r5.anchor: وروى عن أبي العالية قال : التوحيد

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r6.claim: Mujahid says they do not extend their hands in spending for a rightful cause.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : يقبضون ايديهم : لا يبسطونها بنفقة في حق

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r7.claim: Qatada says they withhold their hands from every good.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة : ويقبضون ايديهم قال : يقبضون ايديهم عن كل خير

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r8.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says they withhold their hands from charity and good works.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r8.anchor: وروى عن السدى انه قال : يقبضونها من الصدقة والخير

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that they abandoned God.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : نسوا الله يقول : تركوا الله

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r10.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r10.claim: Al-Suddi says they abandoned obedience to God.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r10.anchor: عن السدى قوله : نسوا الله قال : تركوا طاعة الله

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas explains God's leaving them as withholding His reward and honor from them.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1831#2/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : فنسيهم يقول : تركهم من ثوابه وكرامته

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1833/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1833/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1833/r1.claim: Qatada says they forgot what was good but did not forget evil.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1833/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : فنسيهم نسوا من كان خير ، ولم ينسوا من الشر

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1833/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1833/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1833/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the transgressors as disobedient people.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1833/r2.anchor: ذكر عن سليمان بن حرب عن حماد بن زيد عن ابن جريج عن مجاهد الفاسقون : العاصون

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1833/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1833/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1833/r3.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam glosses the transgressors as liars.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1833/r3.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم في قوله : الفاسقون قال : الكاذبون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r1.claim: The verse prevents hypocrites from assuming that pardon for some includes those who persist in hypocrisy: they share one condition, and differences in outcome require a difference between faith and continued hypocrisy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r1.anchor: يظهر أن تكون هذه الآية احتراسا عن أن يظن المنافقون أن العفو المفروض لطائفة منهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr offers three placements: explanation of the punished group, an independent parenthesis, or a parenthesis together with the next verse before 9:69.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r2.anchor: ففصل هاته الجملة عن التي قبلها : إما لأنها كالبيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r3.claim: Explicitly naming female hypocrites makes clear that the rulings apply equally to both sexes and blocks the assumption that women might be pardoned while only men are punished.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r3.anchor: وزيد في هذه الآية ذكر { المنافقات } تنصيصا على تسوية الأحكام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r4.claim: Min is associative, expressing connection and alliance through figurative partitivity; the verse does not use awliyāʾ as 9:71 does for the believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r4.anchor: و { من } في قوله : { بعضهم من بعض } اتصالية دالة على معنى اتصال شيء بشيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r5.claim: The phrase includes all hypocrites, since each is part of the whole; their mutual connection establishes that they share the same condition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r5.anchor: وقد شمل قوله : { بعضهم من بعض } جميع المنافقين والمنافقات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r6.claim: Their command to do wrong explains what their mutual connection and sameness mean in practice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p253#2/r6.anchor: وجملة { يأمرون بالمنكر } مبينة لمعنى الاتصال والاستواء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r1.claim: This opens a report and divine judgment: the hypocrite men and women share the same status and degree of unbelief, as “ears are part of the head” describes shared legal treatment for wiping.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r1.anchor: هذا ابتداء إخبار عنهم وحكم من الله تعالى عليهم بما تضمنته الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r2.claim: The earlier statement “they are not of you” makes this declaration appropriate; the author compares it with the legal expression that the ears are part of the head for wiping.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r2.anchor: وهذا نحو قولهم الأذنان من الرأس يريدون في حكم المسح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r3.claim: Their enjoining evil means calling to unbelief, worship of other than God, and the other evils named in the verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r3.anchor: وقوله يأمرون بالمنكر يريد بالكفر وعبادة غير الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r4.claim: These hypocrites lacked power and overt public actions because Islam and God’s word had become dominant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r4.anchor: لأن المنافقين الذين نزلت هذه الآيات فيهم لم يكونوا أهل قدرة ولا أفعال ظاهرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r5.claim: Their “withholding hands” refers to withholding charity and good works.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r5.anchor: و «القبض» هو عن الصدقة وفعل الخير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r6.claim: They forgot God by abandoning His Prophet and law; God then left them without guidance or protection from Hell’s punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r6.anchor: أي تركوه حين تركوا نبيه وشرعته فتركهم حين لم يهدهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r7.claim: Calling divine abandonment “forgetting” intensifies the sense of leaving them, as abandonment has reached the degree associated with forgetfulness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r7.anchor: وإنما يعبر بالنسيان عن الترك مبالغة إذا بلغ وجوه الترك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r8.claim: The author compares this sense of nisyān as abandonment with 2:237 and 28:77.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r8.anchor: وعلى هذا يجيء ولا تنسوا الفضل بينكم [البقرة: 237]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r9.claim: Their fisq is the unbelief that entails eternal residence in Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r9.anchor: ثم حكم عليهم عز وجل بالفسق وهو فسوق الكفر المقتضي للخلود في النار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r10.claim: Qatāda says God left them out of good, but did not leave them out of evil.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p55#2/r10.anchor: وكان قتادة يقول فنسيهم أي من الخير ولم ينسهم من الشر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the hypocrites share one religion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r1.anchor: قاله ابن عباس بعضهم على دين بعض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r2.claim: Muqātil explains that hypocrites are allies of one another.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r3.claim: Here the evil they enjoin is unbelief, and the good they forbid is faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r3.anchor: ﴿ يأمرون بالمنكر ﴾ وهو الكفر ﴿ وينهون عن المعروف ﴾ وهو الإيمان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Mujāhid say they withhold their hands from spending in God's cause.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r4.anchor: أحدها يقبضونها عن الإنفاق في سبيل الله قاله ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r5.claim: Qatāda interprets the phrase as withholding their hands from every good deed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r5.anchor: والثاني عن كل خير قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r6.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r6.claim: Al-Māwardī also transmits the interpretation that they withhold their hands from fighting in God's cause.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r6.anchor: والثالث عن الجهاد في سبيل الله والرابع عن رفعها في الدعاء إلى الله تعالى ذكرهما الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r7.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r7.claim: Al-Māwardī also transmits that they refrain from raising their hands in supplication to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r7.anchor: والثالث عن الجهاد في سبيل الله والرابع عن رفعها في الدعاء إلى الله تعالى ذكرهما الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj glosses this as their abandoning God's command, after which He leaves them without His mercy and guidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p467/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج تركوا أمره فتركهم من رحمته وتوفيقه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r1.claim: Hypocrites reverse the believers' moral conduct: they enjoin wrongdoing, forbid right, and withhold their hands from spending for God's cause.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى منكرا على المنافقين الذين هم على خلاف صفات المؤمنين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r2.claim: Their withholding their hands means they refuse to spend in God's cause.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r2.anchor: أي: عن الإنفاق في سبيل الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r3.claim: They forgot to remember God, so He treated them as one treats people who have forgotten; this is like the warning in 45:34.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r3.anchor: {نسوا الله} أي: نسوا ذكر الله، {فنسيهم} أي: عاملهم معاملة من نسيهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r4.claim: Fasiqun are those who leave the path of truth and enter the path of error.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p172#3/r4.anchor: أي: الخارجون عن طريق الحق، الداخلون في طريق الضلالة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the report was not transmitted only by Ḥamza al-Zayyāt: Ibn Isḥāq also relates it through al-Ḥārith al-Aʿwar; although Ḥamza is weak in hadith, he is an eminent reciter, and criticism of al-Ḥārith concerns belief rather than certain deliberate fabrication.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r1.anchor: لم ينفرد بروايته حمزة بن حبيب الزيات، بل قد رواه محمد بن إسحاق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr considers the saying more likely to be ʿAlī’s own words than a Prophetic report, which some mistakenly elevated; he calls it sound in meaning and notes a supporting report from Ibn Masʿūd.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r2.anchor: أن يكون من كلام أمير المؤمنين علي، رضي الله عنه، وقد وهم بعضهم في رفعه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r3.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Masʿūd and the Prophet calls the Qurʾan God’s banquet, rope, manifest light, beneficial healing, protection, and salvation, and promises ten rewards per letter, counting alif, lām, and mīm separately; Ibn Kathīr calls this route gharīb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إن هذا القرآن مأدبة الله تعالى فتعلموا من مأدبته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم الرازي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r4.claim: Abū Ḥātim calls al-Hijrī weak and not strong, while al-Azdī says he frequently raises reports with many errors; Ibn Kathīr suggests the report may have been mistakenly attributed to the Prophet rather than being Ibn Masʿūd’s saying.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r4.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم الرازي: لين ليس بالقوي. وقال أبو الفتح الأزدي: رفاع كثير الوهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a person’s state is known by the Qurʾan: whoever loves the Qurʾan loves God and His Messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p21/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: لا يسأل عبد عن نفسه إلا القرآن، فإن كان يحب القرآن فإنه يحب الله ورسوله

JISHUMI:v5p3189/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r1.claim: Qabḍ is the opposite of spreading or opening; the source notes its noun and forms for a sword’s grip and for dying.
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r1.anchor: القبض: خلاف البسط، وهو مصدر قبضت قبضا، ومقبض السيف: حيث يقبض عليه بكسر الباء وفتحها،

JISHUMI:v5p3189/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r2.claim: Qabṣ with ṣād means taking with fingertips, whereas qabḍ with ḍād means taking with the palm.
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r2.anchor: تناول بأطراف الأصابع، وبالضاد معجمة: تناول الكف،

JISHUMI:v5p3189/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r3.claim: Calling stinginess ‘clenching the hand’ is figurative: a giver opens the hand, so a miser is described as closing it.
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r3.anchor: ويقال للبخل: قبض اليد، وجعد الكف؛ لأن المعطي يبسط يده، فقيل لمن بخل: قبض توسعا.

JISHUMI:v5p3189/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r4.claim: Nisyān is the opposite of remembering and also means leaving or abandoning; the source notes related forms for forgotten belongings and human forgetfulness.
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r4.anchor: والنسيان: خلاف الذكر، والنسي: ما سقط من منازل المرتحلين من رذال أمتعتهم، كأنهم نسوها،

JISHUMI:v5p3189/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r7.speaker: author
