JISHUMI:v5p3189/r7.claim: Min can mark an origin or starting point, as in travel from Basra to Kufa, or a partitive relation, as in a door made of iron.
JISHUMI:v5p3189/r7.anchor: (من) حرف يستعمل في أشياء: تكون لابتداء الغاية، كقولهم: جئت من البصرة إلى الكوفة،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r1.claim: The phrase denies that the hypocrites are believers, refutes their oath that they belong to the believers, and confirms the statement that they are not of them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r1.anchor: أريد به نفي أن يكونوا من المؤمنين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r2.claim: Their conduct is the opposite of believers’: they command unbelief and sins and forbid faith and obedience.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r2.anchor: الكفر والمعاصي { وينهون عن المعروف } عن الإيمان والطاعات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r3.claim: They hold back their hands out of greed, refusing goods, charity, and spending in God’s cause.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r4.claim: They neglected God’s remembrance, so He left them without His mercy and favor.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r4.anchor: أغفلوا ذكره { فنسيهم } فتركهم من رحمته وفضله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r5.claim: They are complete in fisq: rebellion in unbelief and stripping themselves of every good.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r5.anchor: هم الكاملون في الفسق الذي هو التمرد في الكفر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r6.claim: Muslims should be deterred from earning this ugly name, which God uses in emphatic condemnation; the Prophet even disliked a Muslim saying ‘I am lazy,’ since hypocrites are called lazy in 4:142.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p274/r6.anchor: وكفى المسلم زاجرا أن يلم بما يكسبه هذا الاسم الفاحش

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r1.claim: The phrase can mean that hypocrites join one another in hypocrisy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r1.anchor: أن بعضهم يجتمع مع بعض على النفاق

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, they acquire hypocrisy from one another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r2.anchor: أن بعضهم يأخذ نفاقه من بعض

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says they follow one another’s religion.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r4.claim: One explanation takes reprehensible acts as everything reason rejects, such as shirk, and recognized good as everything good reason recognizes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r4.anchor: المنكر كل ما أنكره العقل من الشرك , والمعروف : كل ما عرفه العقل من الخير

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r5.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says that in the Qur’an, recognized good means faith and reprehensible acts mean shirk.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r5.anchor: المعروف في كتاب الله تعالى كله الإيمان , والمنكر في كتاب الله تعالى كله الشرك , قاله أبو العالية

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r6.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r6.claim: They withhold their hands from spending in God’s cause.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r6.anchor: يقبضونها عن الإنفاق في سبيل الله تعالى , قاله الحسن ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r7.claim: Qatāda says they withhold their hands from every good deed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r7.anchor: يقبضونها عن كل خير , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r8.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r8.claim: Some later commentators say they withhold their hands from fighting alongside the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r8.anchor: عن الجهاد مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , قاله بعض المتأخرين

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r9.claim: Another reported interpretation is that they refrain from raising their hands in supplication to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r9.anchor: يقبضون أيديهم عن رفعها في الدعاء إلى الله تعالى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r10.claim: They abandoned God’s command, so He abandoned them to the loss of His mercy.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports 300 male and 170 female hypocrites in Medina.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r11.anchor: كان المنافقون بالمدينة من الرجال ثلاثمائة , ومن النساء سبعين ومائة امرأة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r12.speaker: مكحول عن أبي الدرداء
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r12.claim: Via Makhūl, Abū al-Dardāʾ asks the Prophet about hypocrites; the Prophet lists lying, betrayal, broken promises, abusive quarrels, broken covenants, neglect of prayer, and little remembrance of God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p378#2/r12.anchor: مكحول عن أبي الدرداء أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن صفة المنافق

MUJAHID:v1p283#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p283#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p283#4/r1.claim: Withholding their hands means that the hypocrites do not spend on what is due.
MUJAHID:v1p283#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ ويقبضون أيديهم ﴾ قال لا يبسطونها بالنفقة في حق

MUQATIL:9:67-69/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:67-69/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:67-69/r1.claim: The hypocrite men and women are allies of one another in hypocrisy.

MUQATIL:9:67-69/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:67-69/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:67-69/r2.claim: Their commanding wrong means rejecting Muhammad; forbidding right means opposing faith in Muhammad and what he brought.
MUQATIL:9:67-69/r2.anchor: { يأمرون بالمنكر } ، يعنى بالتكذيب بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، { وينهون عن المعروف } ، يعنى الإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وبما جاء به

MUQATIL:9:67-69/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:67-69/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:67-69/r3.claim: They hold back their hands by withholding spending on good causes.
MUQATIL:9:67-69/r3.anchor: يعنى يمسكون عن النفقة فى خير

MUQATIL:9:67-69/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:67-69/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:67-69/r4.claim: Forgetting God means abandoning work according to His command, including withholding good spending; hypocrites are the disobedient.
MUQATIL:9:67-69/r4.anchor: يقول: تركوا العمل بأمر الله، يمسكون عن النفقة فى خير، { إن المنافقين هم الفاسقون }

NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r1.claim: The source counts three hundred hypocritical men and one hundred seventy hypocritical women.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r1.anchor: الرجال المنافقون كانوا ثلثمائة والنساء المنافقات

NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r2.claim: They are like one self; this denies that they belong to believers and refutes their claim «we are of you», reinforcing «they are not of you».
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r2.anchor: وفيه نفى أن يكونوا من المؤمنين وتكذيبهم فى قولهم ويحلفون بالله إنهم لمنكم وتقرير لقوله وما هم منكم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r3.claim: They command unbelief and disobedience and forbid obedience and faith, opposite to believers.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r3.anchor: بالكفر والعصيان ﴿ وينهون عن المعروف ﴾ عن الطاعة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r4.claim: They withhold out of stinginess alms and spending in God’s path.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r4.anchor: شحا بالمبار والصدقات والإنفاق فى سبيل الله

NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r5.claim: «They forgot God» may mean abandoning His command or neglecting His remembrance.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r6.claim: God’s forgetting them means leaving them without mercy and favor.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r7.claim: They are fully rebellious in unbelief and stripped of every good; Muslims should avoid earning this harsh label.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p97#2/r7.anchor: هم الكاملون فى الفسق الذي هو التمرد فى الكفر والانسلاخ عن كل خير

QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r1.claim: The phrase begins a nominal sentence; baʿḍuhum may begin a second sentence or be a substitute, with min baʿḍ as predicate.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { المنافقون والمنافقات } ابتداء. { بعضهم } ابتداء ثان

QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r2.claim: The hypocrites are like one thing in their departure from religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r2.anchor: ومعنى { بعضهم من بعض } أي هم كالشيء الواحد في الخروج عن الدين

QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r3.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj connects this to hypocrites claiming they belong to believers but do not; they resemble one another in enjoining wrong and forbidding right.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج، هذا متصل بقوله: «يحلفون بالله إنهم لمنكم وما هم منكم»

QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r4.claim: Withholding their hands refers to abandoning jihad and failing to fulfill what is due.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r4.anchor: وقبض أيديهم عبارة عن ترك الجهاد، وفيما يجب عليهم من حق

QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r5.claim: “Forgetting” means neglect: they neglected God’s commands, so He left them in doubt.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r5.anchor: والنسيان: الترك هنا أي تركوا ما أمرهم الله به فتركهم في الشك

QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r6.claim: Another explanation says they neglected God’s command until it seemed forgotten, so God treated them as forgotten with respect to reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r6.anchor: وقيل: إنهم تركوا أمره حتى صار كالمنسي فصيرهم بمنزلة المنسي من ثوابه

QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r7.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r7.claim: Qatādah says God has forgotten them with respect to good, but not evil.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: «نسيهم» أي من الخير فأما من الشر فلم ينسهم

QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:67/r8.claim: Fisq is departure from obedience and religion.

BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r1.claim: The gloss identifies the hypocrites as three hundred men and one hundred seventy women.

BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r2.claim: Male and female hypocrites resemble one another in hypocrisy and distance from faith as parts of a single entity.
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r2.anchor: أي متشابهون في النفاق والبعد عن الإيمان كأبعاض الشيء الواحد بالشخص

BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r3.claim: They command disbelief and acts of disobedience.

BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r4.claim: Their prohibition of faith and obedience resumes and confirms the description and makes their opposition to the believers’ state explicit.
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r4.anchor: أي : عن الإيمان والطاعة استئناف مقرر لمضمون ما سبق

BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r5.claim: Withholding the hands means refusing to spend in God’s cause, give charity, or do any good; it is a figure for stinginess.
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r5.anchor: عن الإنفاق في سبيل الله وعن الصدقة وعن كل خير فإن قبض اليد كناية عن الشح

BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r6.claim: Al-Kashifi also interprets withholding their hands as not raising them in supplication and intimate prayer.
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r6.anchor: أو عن رفعها للدعاء والمناجاة كما في "الكاشفي"

BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r7.claim: Forgetting God means neglecting His remembrance and abandoning His command; forgetting names its consequence, abandonment, because literal forgetfulness is not voluntary and is not blameworthy.
BURSEVI:v3p349#2/r7.anchor: صاروا غافلين عن ذكره وتركوا أمره حتى صار كالمنسي عندهم

BURSEVI:v3p349#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p349#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p349#3/r1.claim: God’s forgetting means leaving them without His grace and favor, not overpowering or punishing them; literal forgetfulness is impossible for God.
BURSEVI:v3p349#3/r1.anchor: فتركهم من لطفه وفضله لا من قهره وتعذيبه وفسر النسيان أيضا بالمعنى المجازي

BURSEVI:v3p349#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p349#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p349#3/r2.claim: The hypocrites are fully rebellious, departing from obedience and stripping away every good.
BURSEVI:v3p349#3/r2.anchor: الكاملون في التمرد والفسق الذي هو الخروج عن الطاعة والانسلاخ عن كل خير

RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r1.claim: Male and female hypocrites share the same qualities of hypocrisy; “some are of some” means their way is one, with no real distinction between them.
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r1.anchor: أنت مني وأنا منك ، أي أمرنا واحد

RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r2.claim: Munkar includes every ugly deed, especially denying the Messenger; maʿrūf includes every good deed, especially belief in the Messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r2.anchor: ولفظ المنكر يدخل فيه كل قبيح

RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r3.claim: Some take “they clench their hands” as withholding every good; Rāzī prefers withholding obligatory charity, including zakat and spending in God’s path, since only abandoning an obligation is censured.
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r3.anchor: وقيل عن كل خير واجب من زكاة وصدقة

RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r4.claim: The image comes from a giver extending an open hand, so a miser who refuses to give is described as closing the hand.

RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r5.claim: The wording cannot mean literal forgetfulness: human forgetfulness is involuntary and does not merit blame, while forgetfulness is impossible for God.
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r5.anchor: لا يمكن إجراؤه على ظاهره لأنا لو حملناه على النسيان على الحقيقة لما استحقوا عليه ذما

RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r6.claim: One interpretation is that they abandoned God’s command until it was like something forgotten, so He left them as forgotten with respect to reward and mercy; the wording parallels the “evil recompense” in 42:40.
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r6.anchor: تركوا أمره حتى صار بمنزلة المنسي

RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r7.claim: Another interpretation makes forgetting the opposite of remembering: they left worship and praise of God, so He left remembering them with mercy and kindness; “forgetting” names the consequence of not remembering.
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r7.anchor: فلما تركوا ذكر الله بالعبادة والثناء على الله

RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p101/r8.claim: Calling the hypocrites fāsiqūn means they are complete or extreme in their impiety.
